phases.name: Freeze the brief and establish a governed upload path
phases.description: Keep the supplied targets separate from workload assumptions, then establish tenant identity, upload control, and a direct-to-storage file path.

phases.name: Store originals and dispatch idempotent processing work
phases.description: Preserve original bytes, emit durable work notifications, and consume them with bounded workers while keeping queue delay inside the measured latency budget.

phases.name: Classify, extract, validate, and persist results
phases.description: Use the managed document processors for OCR and structured extraction, validate values and confidence explicitly, and persist a traceable result record.

phases.name: Route uncertain cases for review and isolate failures
phases.description: Keep low-confidence business exceptions distinct from transient failures, support authenticated human correction, and make retries safe.

phases.name: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
phases.description: Build operational and labeled-quality evidence, then turn the brief's targets into load-test and release gates rather than architecture promises.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and establish a governed upload path
steps.title: Freeze the exact problem brief and mark unknowns
steps.content: Live brief: Build an Intelligent Document Processing Pipeline. Description: Design a document processing system that extracts text from PDFs and images, classifies documents, extracts structured data, and validates accuracy. Explicit requirements: Extract text from documents; Classify document types; Extract entities and fields; Process invoices and receipts; Validate extracted data; Store structured results; Handle various document formats; Monitor processing accuracy. Explicit constraints: Processing time under 10 seconds per doc; Support 100k+ documents per day; Extraction accuracy above 95%; Handle PDFs, images, and scanned docs; Cost-effective at scale. Supplied hints: Document AI for OCR and extraction; Cloud Functions for orchestration; Cloud Storage for document storage; Firestore for structured data; Vision API for image analysis; AutoML for custom models. Design assumptions to confirm: one tenant-aware upload/status API; the ten-second target is measured from accepted upload to a validated result for a bounded, agreed document envelope; the accuracy target is evaluated against human-labeled examples by document type and field; 100k/day is a daily volume, not a known peak rate. The brief does not specify page/file-size limits, region, burst profile, languages, retention, or the exact accuracy metric. Do not claim these targets are already achieved.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and establish a governed upload path
steps.title: Give submitters and reviewers one governed workspace
steps.content: Use a thin web client for upload initiation, job status, and reviewer work. The browser should send document bytes directly to a short-lived signed Cloud Storage URL, not proxy large files through the application tier. Show a durable job ID and an explicit pending, completed, needs-review, or failed state.

component.label: Submitter & Reviewer Workspace
component.description: Authenticated document upload, status, and human-review UI

properties.purpose: Let authorized users initiate uploads, view job status and validated structured results, and correct low-confidence fields through a human-review workflow.

component.highlightReason: The user-facing flow is separate from file transfer and background processing, while still exposing review and result states.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and establish a governed upload path
steps.title: Scope every document and result to a tenant
steps.content: Authenticate submitters, reviewers, and service identities separately. Enforce tenant and role authorization in the API and data access path; never trust a tenant ID supplied only by the browser. Use short-lived service credentials and audit reviewer corrections.

component.label: Tenant Identity & Access Policy

properties.purpose: Authenticate submitters and reviewers, enforce tenant and role checks server-side, and provide workload identity for service-to-service calls.

component.highlightReason: Documents and extracted fields can contain sensitive data, so identity and tenant boundaries must be explicit.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and establish a governed upload path
steps.title: Expose a small authenticated control API
steps.content: The gateway handles upload-intent creation, status/result reads, and reviewer actions. Validate MIME type and declared size at initiation, apply per-tenant quotas, and require an idempotency key so retries cannot create duplicate logical jobs. It returns a short-lived signed upload URL rather than carrying the file body.

component.label: Upload, Status & Review API Gateway
component.description: Authenticated control plane for document jobs

properties.purpose: Expose tenant-scoped upload-intent, status/result, and reviewer endpoints with request validation, throttling, and idempotency; keep document bytes off this control plane.

component.highlightReason: Separating control requests from file transfer protects the API tier and gives retries a stable job identity.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and establish a governed upload path
steps.title: Create an upload intent before accepting bytes
steps.content: Use a small Cloud Functions handler to authorize the tenant, validate the allowed format envelope, create an idempotent job record, and issue a short-lived signed upload URL. Keep this function out of the OCR path; its response should not wait for document processing.

component.label: Upload Intent & Job Coordinator
component.description: Cloud Functions control handler for upload admission

properties.purpose: Create or return an idempotent tenant-scoped job, validate the supported upload envelope, and issue a short-lived signed Cloud Storage upload URL.

component.highlightReason: Cloud Functions is used for lightweight event/control orchestration, not as a proxy for large file uploads.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and establish a governed upload path
steps.title: Start uploads through the authenticated control plane
steps.content: The portal first requests an upload intent and later polls or subscribes to the job status through the authenticated API.

connection.label: Create upload intent / read status
connection.description: Tenant-authenticated API requests carry metadata and idempotency keys, never the document body.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and establish a governed upload path
steps.title: Authorize the caller before issuing storage access
steps.content: The API validates the caller's scoped identity and derives the tenant boundary server-side before creating an upload intent or returning results.

connection.label: Validate identity and tenant scope
connection.description: Only authorized roles receive upload, result-read, or reviewer permissions.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and establish a governed upload path
steps.title: Keep upload admission idempotent and bounded
steps.content: The gateway calls the coordinator with tenant, declared format, checksum metadata, and an idempotency key. Validate the actual object after upload as well; client-provided MIME and size are not trusted evidence.

connection.label: Create or resume upload job
connection.description: Admission returns a stable job ID and a narrowly scoped, expiring upload capability.

steps.phase: Freeze the brief and establish a governed upload path
steps.title: Choose safe defaults for the control plane
steps.content: Use JWT-authenticated, tenant-scoped requests with server-side MIME/size validation, throttling, and idempotency. Treat direct object upload as a narrowly scoped capability, not a reusable credential.

decision.question: How should upload and review operations be exposed?
decision.chosen: Authenticated API control plane plus short-lived signed object uploads
decision.chosenReason: It avoids proxying large files through the API and allows job creation, result reads, and reviewer actions to share one auditable authorization boundary.

alternatives.option: Send file bytes through the API gateway
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler client flow but increases API memory, timeout, and cost pressure.
Avoids signed URL issuance but expands the blast radius and complicates revocation.

steps.phase: Store originals and dispatch idempotent processing work
steps.title: Keep immutable source documents in Cloud Storage
steps.content: Store the original bytes in a tenant-scoped Cloud Storage bucket and retain a checksum, object generation, content type, and upload timestamp with the job. Define retention and lifecycle policy from the product's privacy requirements; do not invent a retention duration from this brief.

component.label: Cloud Storage: Original Documents
component.description: Durable source files partitioned by tenant and job

properties.purpose: Store original PDFs and supported image files under tenant-scoped object paths with checksums, generation IDs, least-privilege access, and a policy-defined lifecycle.

component.highlightReason: Original bytes are the durable replay and audit source; extracted fields are derived data and never replace them.

steps.phase: Store originals and dispatch idempotent processing work
steps.title: Issue a constrained upload capability
steps.content: The coordinator scopes the signed URL to one tenant/job object and a short expiry. The object path and metadata are server-generated; upload completion is verified against the expected checksum and actual content.

connection.label: Issue scoped object upload URL
connection.description: The coordinator controls object naming and authorization without receiving the file bytes.

steps.phase: Store originals and dispatch idempotent processing work
steps.title: Transfer document bytes directly to the bucket
steps.content: The browser uploads directly to the authorized object path and reports the resulting object generation. The backend verifies the object and checksum before marking it eligible for processing.

connection.label: Upload original PDF or image
connection.description: Large bodies bypass the application servers while tenant scope, expiry, and object integrity remain enforced.

steps.phase: Store originals and dispatch idempotent processing work
steps.title: Separate document arrival from processing execution
steps.content: Publish one job event per verified object generation. Include job ID, tenant ID, object URI/generation, checksum, and an event version—not extracted content or secrets. Consumers must be idempotent because delivery may be repeated.

component.label: Document Processing Events (Pub/Sub)
component.description: Durable event handoff from verified upload to workers

properties.purpose: Deliver versioned, idempotent object-ready events to processing workers with durable retention and controlled replay.

component.highlightReason: A durable event boundary absorbs arrival bursts and makes retries explicit, but its backlog still counts against the processing-time target.

steps.phase: Store originals and dispatch idempotent processing work
steps.title: Trigger work only after an object is verified
steps.content: A verified Cloud Storage object-created event is converted to the versioned processing message. Ignore duplicate notifications for the same job and object generation.

connection.label: Publish verified document job
connection.description: Only accepted objects enter the processing pipeline; event identity supports deduplication.

steps.phase: Store originals and dispatch idempotent processing work
steps.title: Consume jobs with bounded Cloud Functions workers
steps.content: Use an event-triggered Cloud Functions worker to load the object, select the applicable processor, and carry a deadline and trace ID through each call. Keep the worker stateless; persist progress and use idempotency keys so retries do not create duplicate result records.

component.label: Document Processing Worker
component.description: Cloud Functions consumer and per-document orchestrator

properties.purpose: Consume verified document events, retrieve the exact object generation, select a processor, enforce a per-job deadline, and persist idempotent progress.

component.highlightReason: A stateless worker can scale with backlog, while its concurrency must respect Document AI quotas and the latency budget.

steps.phase: Store originals and dispatch idempotent processing work
steps.title: Dispatch each job to a processing consumer
steps.content: The consumer acknowledges only after its durable state transition is recorded. Bound retries and use the job ID plus object generation as the idempotency identity.

connection.label: Deliver document job
connection.description: Workers process duplicate deliveries safely and expose queue age as part of end-to-end latency.

steps.phase: Store originals and dispatch idempotent processing work
steps.title: Read the exact immutable source generation
steps.content: The worker fetches the object generation referenced by the message, verifies the checksum, and records which bytes were processed. This prevents a later overwrite from silently changing the meaning of a retry.

connection.label: Read and verify original bytes
connection.description: The original object remains the replayable source of truth for each processing attempt.

steps.phase: Store originals and dispatch idempotent processing work
steps.title: Make retries durable without hiding queue delay
steps.content: Use durable at-least-once delivery and bounded exponential retry for transient provider errors. Include oldest-job age and upload-to-result time in the same SLO view; an unbounded queue does not satisfy the ten-second target.

decision.question: How should worker retries and bursts be handled?
decision.chosen: Durable Pub/Sub events, idempotent workers, bounded retries, and measured backpressure
decision.chosenReason: This recovers transient failures without pretending that queueing is free latency or allowing duplicate processing to overwrite a newer result.

alternatives.option: Drop work when workers are busy
alternatives.tradeoff: Protects worker latency but loses accepted documents and makes completion unreliable.

alternatives.option: Retry indefinitely in the hot path
alternatives.tradeoff: Can amplify outages and make per-document completion time unbounded.

steps.phase: Classify, extract, validate, and persist results
steps.title: Use Document AI as the primary document processor
steps.content: The existing catalog has no Google Document AI processor entry, so this is the one intentional custom node. Use the appropriate processor set: OCR/layout for text, a classifier for document type, Invoice Parser for invoices, and a suitable extractor for receipts and other supported fields. Return source spans, normalized entities, and per-field confidence when available; retain the processor and version IDs with each result.

component.label: Google Document AI: OCR, Classification & Extraction
component.description: Managed OCR, document classification, invoice parsing, and structured field extraction

properties.componentName: Google Document AI: OCR, Classification & Extraction
properties.purpose: Process supported PDFs and images with OCR/layout, classify document types, use the Invoice Parser for invoices, and extract configured fields for receipts and other classes while returning traceable processor/version and confidence metadata.
properties.componentType: Google-managed document OCR, classifier, invoice parser, and extraction processors (catalog gap)
properties.notes: Use processor-specific format/page limits and a bounded online-processing envelope for the sub-10-second target. Batch processing is not the latency path. Measure field-level accuracy against reviewed labels; low-confidence or invalid results go to human review.

component.highlightReason: Document AI combines document OCR, classification, and entity extraction; no existing catalog component expresses this managed GCP service.

steps.phase: Classify, extract, validate, and persist results
steps.title: Send the verified document to the selected processor
steps.content: The worker selects a processor using the verified format and document class, passes only the required object reference/content, and enforces a request deadline and bounded retry policy.

connection.label: Classify and extract document fields
connection.description: Processor choice is explicit and versioned for each attempt; no second OCR engine is invoked by default.

steps.phase: Classify, extract, validate, and persist results
steps.title: Validate extracted fields before they become results
steps.content: Use a separate Cloud Functions validation step for schema/type checks, required-field rules, normalization, cross-field checks, and business invariants such as totals matching line items. Preserve raw extraction and source evidence; never silently coerce an invalid value into a confident result.

component.label: Field Validation & Review Router
component.description: Cloud Functions validation and confidence-based routing

properties.purpose: Validate extracted schemas, required fields, types, confidence thresholds, and cross-field business rules; route valid outputs to persistence and uncertain cases to human review.

component.highlightReason: OCR output is a candidate result, not a trusted business record until deterministic validation and confidence policy pass.

steps.phase: Classify, extract, validate, and persist results
steps.title: Pass structured fields and confidence into validation
steps.content: Pass document type, normalized fields, per-field confidence, source spans, processor/version, and job identity to validation. Keep enough provenance to explain and reproduce a disputed extraction.

connection.label: Fields, confidence and source evidence
connection.description: The validator receives both values and evidence rather than treating model output as ground truth.

steps.phase: Classify, extract, validate, and persist results
steps.title: Route by document type instead of running every model
steps.content: Use Document AI classification to select the smallest suitable processor: the invoice parser for invoices, a receipt/custom extractor for receipts, and a configured processor for other supported classes. The hint mentions Cloud Vision and AutoML, but neither should duplicate the default document path: Google recommends Document AI for scanned-document OCR, parsing, and entity extraction. Add Vision for a separately demonstrated image-analysis need; evaluate a separate custom model only when labeled results show a gap that the Document AI processor cannot meet.

decision.question: Should every document call OCR, Vision, AutoML, and extraction in sequence?
decision.chosen: Route to one fit-for-purpose Document AI processor, and add another model only for a measured residual need
decision.chosenReason: Serially invoking overlapping models adds latency and cost without guaranteeing higher field accuracy. Document AI already covers the core document OCR/classification/extraction path.

alternatives.option: Run Vision OCR and Document AI OCR for every file
alternatives.tradeoff: Duplicates OCR work and increases latency/cost; keep Vision for a distinct image-analysis use case.

alternatives.option: Add an AutoML classifier before Document AI by default
alternatives.tradeoff: Adds another model call and maintenance surface before evidence shows a classification gap.

properties.notes: Primary path: Document AI OCR/layout plus type-specific classifier/extractor (Invoice Parser for invoices, suitable receipt/custom extractor for receipts). Cloud Vision or a separate AutoML/Vertex model is an evaluated optional alternative only when it addresses a distinct measured gap; do not serially duplicate OCR by default. Check processor-specific format, size, page, region, and quota limits before choosing the online path.

steps.phase: Classify, extract, validate, and persist results
steps.title: Persist validated structured output in Firestore
steps.content: Store one tenant-scoped job/result record keyed by stable job ID and object generation. Persist status, document class, normalized fields, validation outcomes, confidence/evidence references, processor version, timestamps, and correction history. Use conditional/idempotent updates so repeated events cannot move a completed job backward.

component.label: Firestore: Job State & Structured Results
component.description: Tenant-scoped operational records and extracted fields

properties.purpose: Persist tenant-scoped job state, validated structured fields, processor provenance, review status, and correction history with idempotent state transitions.

component.highlightReason: Firestore is the operational source for status and structured results; analytical accuracy aggregates belong in BigQuery.

steps.phase: Classify, extract, validate, and persist results
steps.title: Commit only validated or explicitly review-pending output
steps.content: Write a validated result atomically with its job state, or persist a review-pending state with the reason and evidence references. Use conditional writes or transactions for state transitions; do not report a job as complete before the durable commit succeeds.

connection.label: Commit result and processing state
connection.description: The durable record distinguishes validated output from incomplete, rejected, or human-review work.

steps.phase: Classify, extract, validate, and persist results
steps.title: Do not turn model confidence into an accuracy claim
steps.content: A confidence threshold is a routing signal, not proof of >95% accuracy. Combine required-field checks, cross-field rules, processor confidence, and document-class policy. Persist the reason for each manual-review route and avoid silently accepting low-confidence values.

decision.question: What should happen when extraction is incomplete, inconsistent, or low confidence?
decision.chosen: Mark the job needs-review and preserve the extracted values with field-level evidence
decision.chosenReason: Review preserves useful machine output while preventing uncertain values from being presented as validated business data.

alternatives.tradeoff: Improves apparent automation rate but can silently corrupt structured records.

alternatives.option: Reject every document with one uncertain field
alternatives.tradeoff: Protects correctness but creates avoidable rework; field-aware review can focus human effort.

properties.purpose: Validate schemas, required fields, types, confidence thresholds, and business invariants; persist valid output, and route uncertain or inconsistent fields to review with values and evidence preserved. Confidence is a routing signal, not measured accuracy.

steps.phase: Route uncertain cases for review and isolate failures
steps.title: Queue business uncertainty for human review
steps.content: Create a durable reviewer task only for low-confidence, missing, or cross-field-inconsistent cases. Include the job ID, field-level reason, and source location, but avoid copying unnecessary raw document data into queue messages.

component.label: Low-Confidence Human Review Queue
component.description: Durable work queue for uncertain extraction fields

properties.purpose: Hold review tasks for documents with uncertain fields, failed business rules, or unsupported classes until an authorized reviewer resolves them.

component.highlightReason: Human review handles semantic uncertainty; it is separate from retrying a transient service failure.

steps.phase: Route uncertain cases for review and isolate failures
steps.title: Route exceptions without blocking healthy documents
steps.content: The validator sends a compact review task when fields fail confidence or business rules. Other documents continue through the normal path; a human decision is not required for every successful extraction.

connection.label: Queue uncertain fields for review
connection.description: Review tasks include evidence and reason codes while avoiding an unnecessary copy of document bytes.

steps.phase: Route uncertain cases for review and isolate failures
steps.title: Give reviewers a scoped correction interface
steps.content: The reviewer sees the source document or a permission-checked preview, extracted value, confidence, and the reason for review. Record who changed what and when. Human corrections become labeled evidence only after reviewer confirmation.

component.label: Document Review Workbench
component.description: Role-scoped source preview and field correction UI

properties.purpose: Let authorized reviewers inspect source evidence, correct uncertain extracted fields, confirm document type, and record an auditable disposition.

component.highlightReason: The accuracy feedback loop needs accountable human labels, not unverified auto-generated outcomes.

steps.phase: Route uncertain cases for review and isolate failures
steps.title: Claim review work with a lease
steps.content: Review tasks are claimed with a bounded lease so abandoned sessions return to the queue. A claim is not a permanent ownership transfer; reviewer actions are idempotent and tenant-scoped.

connection.label: Claim task and load source evidence
connection.description: Queue leases prevent abandoned work from disappearing and support concurrent reviewer operation.

steps.phase: Route uncertain cases for review and isolate failures
steps.title: Submit corrections through the same authorization boundary
steps.content: The reviewer workspace submits a field correction and disposition through the control API. Require a revision/version token so two reviewers cannot silently overwrite one another.

connection.label: Submit reviewed fields and disposition
connection.description: Reviewer edits use role checks, optimistic concurrency, and an auditable request identity.

steps.phase: Route uncertain cases for review and isolate failures
steps.title: Validate reviewer edits before committing them
steps.content: The same validation service rechecks corrected fields, verifies the expected record revision, and records reviewer identity and change provenance before updating the result.

connection.label: Revalidate human-confirmed fields
connection.description: Human input follows the same schema and business-rule checks as machine output.

steps.phase: Route uncertain cases for review and isolate failures
steps.title: Separate transient processing failure from review work
steps.content: Use a separate dead-letter/quarantine queue for exhausted retries, invalid payloads, or persistent provider errors. Store a reason code and safe replay metadata; never mix operational failures with documents that simply need a person to verify a field.

component.label: Retry Exhaustion & Dead-Letter Queue
component.description: Quarantine for exhausted or malformed processing jobs

properties.purpose: Quarantine exhausted transient failures and malformed jobs with reason codes, attempt counts, and safe replay metadata for operator investigation.

component.highlightReason: Operational failure recovery is a different workflow from semantic low-confidence review.

steps.phase: Route uncertain cases for review and isolate failures
steps.title: Quarantine exhausted failures with replay evidence
steps.content: Only retryable or persistent operational failures enter this queue after a bounded policy. Preserve job/object generation, error class, attempt count, and trace ID; redact document contents from diagnostic messages.

connection.label: Quarantine exhausted processing failure
connection.description: A safe replay starts from the immutable original and never skips validation.

steps.phase: Route uncertain cases for review and isolate failures
steps.title: Replay only after an operator resolves the cause
steps.content: An authorized operator redrives the safe job envelope to Pub/Sub after the upstream issue is understood. Preserve attempt history and use the same job/object idempotency key; do not automatically loop poison messages.

connection.label: Replay resolved processing job
connection.description: Controlled redrive keeps failure evidence and prevents unbounded poison-message loops.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Build a labeled quality and cost evidence set
steps.content: Use BigQuery for versioned, access-controlled aggregate processing events and human-reviewed labels. Measure extraction quality by document class and field against a representative held-out set; track exact-match/precision/recall or the agreed metric, sample count, and confidence interval. Never label model confidence as observed accuracy.

component.label: BigQuery: Quality & Cost Evidence
component.description: Aggregated processor outcomes, reviewed labels, and cost measures

properties.purpose: Analyze redacted job outcomes and human-reviewed labels by document type, field, processor version, latency, review rate, and estimated cost per successfully validated document.

component.highlightReason: The >95% target can only be assessed against reviewed ground truth with a defined metric and representative document mix.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Record outcomes and evidence without copying raw files
steps.content: Emit redacted metrics and references: document class, field outcome, processor/version, confidence band, validation reason, review result, timing, retry count, and cost dimensions. Keep raw documents and sensitive extracted values under the approved data-access policy rather than duplicating them into analytics events.

connection.label: Publish outcome and evidence metadata
connection.description: Aggregate operational and labeled quality evidence while minimizing sensitive-data duplication.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Observe the complete processing journey
steps.content: Instrument upload acceptance, queue age, processor latency/errors, validation outcomes, review backlog, result-commit failures, and cost per validated document. Use trace/job IDs across API, Pub/Sub, functions, Firestore, and Document AI; redact content and tenant secrets from logs.

component.label: Pipeline SLO & Accuracy Monitoring
component.description: Operational metrics, alerts, traces, and quality signals

properties.purpose: Track accepted-to-result latency, queue age, processor errors, validated/review/rejected counts, per-field accuracy evidence, review backlog, and cost per validated document; alert on SLO risk without logging document contents.

component.highlightReason: A pipeline can be connected and still fail silently; operational SLOs and measured extraction quality are separate signals.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Trace worker and processor latency
steps.content: Publish queue wait, processor call duration, retry/error class, and end-to-end job duration. Alert before the ten-second objective is breached, not only after the hard failure threshold.

connection.label: Queue age, processor latency and errors
connection.description: Per-stage spans distinguish service slowness from an arrival burst or downstream quota limit.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Alert on aging review work
steps.content: Track review queue depth and oldest-task age alongside machine processing time. A high automation rate is not a quality win if uncertain documents wait indefinitely or are incorrectly auto-accepted.

connection.label: Review depth and oldest task age
connection.description: Operational review backlog is visible and can trigger staffing or routing action.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Keep observed accuracy distinct from service health
steps.content: Publish aggregate labeled-quality results and sample coverage to monitoring only after the evaluation job has enough reviewed examples. Operationally healthy processors can still miss the accuracy target.

connection.label: Measured accuracy, coverage and unit cost
connection.description: Quality dashboards expose label coverage and evaluation version so percentages cannot be mistaken for unsupported claims.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Read status and results from the durable job record
steps.content: The API returns only the tenant-authorized job state and validated fields, with an explicit needs-review state when applicable. Use revision-aware reads so clients do not display stale results after a reviewer correction.

connection.label: Load job status and validated fields
connection.description: Firestore is the operational read source; analytics queries do not serve user-facing job status.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Show validated output with its actual state
steps.content: Return the result, job state, and field-level review indicators to the authorized user. Do not present queued or partial extraction as completed structured output.

connection.label: Display result or explicit review state
connection.description: The UI distinguishes completed, pending review, rejected, and failed jobs.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Turn the ten-second target into a testable contract
steps.content: The brief says under ten seconds per document but does not define percentile, page count, file size, or whether time ends at extraction or validated result. Provisional acceptance: measure accepted-upload to durable validated-result time for an agreed supported file envelope, include queue wait/retries, and report the full distribution. Do not claim a ten-second guarantee until load tests cover that envelope and actual processor quotas. Keep long-running batch processing off this latency lane.

decision.question: What does 'under 10 seconds per document' mean operationally?
decision.chosen: Use an explicitly agreed end-to-end completion metric and bounded supported-document envelope; keep batch jobs separate
decision.chosenReason: A processor-only timing would omit queue and persistence delay, while an unspecified percentile and file envelope make the target impossible to verify honestly.

alternatives.option: Measure only the Document AI API call
alternatives.tradeoff: Hides upload, queue, validation, and durable-write latency from the user-visible objective.

alternatives.option: Send all files to asynchronous batch processing
alternatives.tradeoff: Can handle larger jobs, but batch completion is not a sub-ten-second interactive guarantee.

properties.purpose: Consume verified jobs and enforce the measured end-to-end deadline, including queue wait, processor calls, validation, and durable result commit. Use the bounded online processor path for the agreed sub-10-second file envelope; divert out-of-envelope work explicitly and do not count it as meeting the latency target.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Make >95% accuracy a labeled release gate
steps.content: Define the accuracy measure with product owners—such as exact field match or precision/recall—then maintain a representative human-labeled holdout by document type, language, and scan quality. Track sample counts and confidence intervals; release a processor version only when the agreed metric exceeds 95% and required classes/fields meet their own floors. Continue sampling after release for drift.

decision.question: How do we know extraction accuracy is above 95%?
decision.chosen: Evaluate processor versions against a representative, human-labeled holdout and monitor post-release drift
decision.chosenReason: Confidence scores and successful HTTP responses are not labels; only comparison to reviewed ground truth measures extraction correctness.

alternatives.option: Use the model's confidence as accuracy
alternatives.tradeoff: Confidence may be miscalibrated and does not show whether the extracted value is correct.

alternatives.option: Pool all fields into one score
alternatives.tradeoff: Can hide poor performance on receipts, rare classes, or critical fields behind common easy cases.

properties.purpose: Measure the agreed field-level quality metric on versioned, human-labeled holdout data by document class, language, scan quality, and processor version; publish sample coverage and confidence intervals, and track cost per successfully validated document.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Load-test the 100k/day target and the unknown burst
steps.content: The daily target averages about 1.16 documents/second if arrivals are uniform, but peak burst, pages/document, processor mix, and regional quotas are not supplied. Load-test realistic and burst workloads; verify per-processor Document AI quotas and request increases where needed before increasing consumer concurrency.

scaleTrigger.metric: Accepted documents/day, peak arrival rate, Pub/Sub oldest-message age, and per-processor quota utilization
scaleTrigger.action: Increase worker concurrency only while processor quotas and the end-to-end latency/error budgets remain healthy; otherwise apply tenant-aware admission control and visible backpressure.
scaleTrigger.impact: Protects the 100k+/day capacity goal without creating quota-throttling retries that break the under-10-second target.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Control document envelopes and cost per useful result
steps.content: Allowlist formats supported by the selected processor (for example PDF, JPEG, PNG, and TIFF where that processor supports them); validate file signatures, scan quality, page/size limits, and language before processing. Measure cost per successfully validated document, including retries and human review. Apply lifecycle policy to originals only after retention/privacy requirements are agreed. Google recommends Document AI for scanned-document OCR and structured extraction; use Cloud Vision only for a distinct image-analysis need, not as a duplicate OCR hop.

decision.question: How do we meet broad format support and cost-effective operation without overclaiming?
decision.chosen: Publish a processor-specific allowlist, route only necessary processor calls, and measure full unit cost including review
decision.chosenReason: Supported file formats and limits differ by processor; an explicit envelope prevents unsupported files and repeated expensive retries from becoming hidden failures.

alternatives.option: Accept every file extension and let the processor decide
alternatives.tradeoff: Creates avoidable failures, long retries, and confusing user experience for unsupported inputs.

alternatives.option: Run every available model on every document
alternatives.tradeoff: Raises latency and spend without evidence that all model outputs are needed.

properties.purpose: Store original, signature-verified, processor-supported PDF/image objects with checksums and tenant-scoped access; apply a lifecycle policy only after retention requirements are approved and measure retained storage cost.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Keep targets, assumptions, and measured results separate
steps.content: This architecture is a design proposal, not proof of capacity, latency, cost, or >95% extraction accuracy. Before production claims, freeze the supported document envelope and accuracy definition, test representative invoices/receipts/scans and burst traffic, review quotas and regional/data-residency requirements, and publish the measured results with sample coverage.

steps.phase: Measure quality, latency, scale, and cost before claiming success
steps.title: Review the complete request and feedback loop
steps.content: Walk the graph end to end: a tenant-authorized upload intent grants direct, bounded object storage; a verified object emits an idempotent event; a worker selects a Document AI processor; validation either commits a traceable structured result or sends uncertainty to a reviewer; transient failures are isolated for controlled replay; and labeled outcomes feed quality, SLO, capacity, and cost evidence. Confirm supported file limits, burst profile, retention, accuracy metric, and review staffing before treating any supplied target as met.
